problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a collection of archival boxes into identical shipping crates. The boxes are categorized as follows:

* Archive Alpha: mass 51 units
* Archive Beta: mass 63 units
* Archive Gamma: mass 44 units
* Archive Delta: mass 32 units
* Archive Epsilon: mass 53 units
* Archive Zeta: mass 62 units
* Archive Eta: mass 46 units
* Archive Theta: mass 55 units
* Archive Iota: mass 64 units
* Archive Kappa: mass 68 units
* Archive Lambda: mass 36 units
* Archive Mu: mass 49 units
* Archive Nu: mass 38 units
* Archive Xi: mass 62 units
* Archive Omicron: mass 38 units
* Archive Pi: mass 39 units
* Archive Rho: mass 34 units
* Archive Sigma: mass 51 units
* Archive Tau: mass 42 units
* Archive Upsilon: mass 32 units
* Archive Phi: mass 31 units
* Archive Chi: mass 61 units
* Archive Psi: mass 60 units
* Archive Omega: mass 34 units
* Archive Cygnus: mass 66 units
* Archive Lyra: mass 63 units
* Archive Draco: mass 33 units
* Archive Orion: mass 38 units
* Archive Vela: mass 70 units

Each shipping crate possesses a maximum load capacity of 100 mass units. The coordinator must place every archival box into exactly one crate, ensuring the aggregate mass within any given crate does not surpass its stipulated limit. The objective is to complete this allocation utilizing the minimal possible number of crates.
